### Ticket Type

🐛 Bug Report (Something isn't working)

### Environment & System Info

```Shell
main 3f797de5952432284a7c77ad2760218cb74e2f26; Windows; Python 3.12.14; torch 2.11.0+cpu. Offline exception-injection tests; no model download or robot required.
```

### Description

`make_policy(cfg, ..., pretrained_path=resume_checkpoint)` temporarily replaces `cfg.pretrained_path` so constructors load from the resume checkpoint, then restores the original parent model on success. If feature preparation, `from_pretrained`, or deferred construction raises, that restoration is skipped.

The caller retains the same config object but its parent path now names the failed checkpoint. A notebook/service catching the exception and retrying with that config can therefore select the wrong source or lose the parent-model provenance. This is about reusing a config after an exception; I am not claiming the ordinary successful training path is broken.

Reproduced on current main 3f797de5952432284a7c77ad2760218cb74e2f26. The proposed patch puts restoration in `finally`, retaining the original exception and the existing successful policy-config restoration. Most changed lines are indentation of the existing construction block. Other config fields are not rolled back.

AI disclosure: investigated, implemented, and locally tested with Codex assistance.


### Context & Reproduction

This injects a loader failure without downloading a model:

```python
from types import SimpleNamespace
from unittest.mock import patch
import lerobot.policies.factory as factory

cfg = SimpleNamespace(
    type="mock", device="cpu", pretrained_path="user/base-policy",
    pretrained_revision=None, use_peft=False, input_features={}, output_features={},
)
def fail(**kwargs):
    raise RuntimeError("resume failed")

with patch.object(factory, "get_policy_class", return_value=SimpleNamespace(from_pretrained=fail)), \
     patch.object(factory, "dataset_to_policy_features", return_value={}):
    try:
        factory.make_policy(
            cfg, ds_meta=SimpleNamespace(features={}, stats={}),
            pretrained_path="run/checkpoints/000002/pretrained_model",
        )
    except RuntimeError:
        pass
assert cfg.pretrained_path == "user/base-policy"  # fails on main
```

The regression patch covers failures in feature conversion, weight loading, and deferred construction. All three fail before the fix and pass after it. The original exception object is also checked.

The two relevant factory test files finish with 28 passes and one existing Windows-only expectation failure: `test_make_policy_loads_resume_weights_and_keeps_the_parent` compares `str(Path(...))` with a forward-slash literal. Restoring main's factory source and rerunning that existing test reproduces the same separator mismatch. Ruff lint and format checks pass.

`pre-commit run mypy --all-files` checked 622 source files and reported nine platform-attribute errors in the untouched `utils/keyboard_input.py` and `rollout/status.py` (`termios`/`tty` and `os.sysconf` on Windows). It reported no errors in `factory.py`; the repository-wide typing check is not green in this environment. No hardware, network download failure, or full training run was exercised; the failure stages are injected by the regression tests.


### Relevant logs or stack trace

```Shell

```

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched existing tickets to ensure this isn't a duplicate.
- [x] I am using the latest version of the `main` branch.
- [ ] I have verified this is not an environment-specific problem.

### Additional Info / Workarounds

Workaround: preserve the original path and restore it in a caller-side finally block when retrying with the same config. Proposed source fix and regression tests:
